cultural_notes: Austin sits on the Balcones Escarpment, the fault line where the Blackland Prairie gives way to the limestone Hill Country -- the reason native limestone is the region's signature building stone (source: texashillcountry.com/limestone-buildings-hill-country; architectgpt.io Texas Hill Country architecture)

Hill Country vernacular architecture draws on German and Hispanic building traditions carried by 19th-century settlers: low-pitched metal roofs, deep covered porches, native limestone walls, casement windows set for the breeze (source: build-construct.com residential construction in Texas Hill Country small towns)

H-E-B holds close to half the Austin-area grocery market and Central Market -- H-E-B's upscale banner -- was founded in Austin in 1994; the local-grocer loyalty is a cultural fact, not just a retail one (source: axios.com H-E-B dominates Austin; en.wikipedia.org Central Market Texas)

Fredericksburg, in the Hill Country west of Austin, runs a peach season mid-May through mid-August that fills roadside stands -- a regional summer ritual (source: visitfredericksburgtx.com peach picking)
